wiki_text: On April 2, 2026, PV Gas completed an upgrade of the Thi Vai LNG terminal's regasification send-out from 171 tonnes per hour to 288 tonnes per hour (approximately 9.5 million cubic meters per day), following commissioning trials in March-April 2026 verified by DNV. PV Gas described the uprate as operation beyond the terminal's original design specifications to meet peak power demand; the terminal's nameplate capacity remains 1 mtpa.

In February 2025 Petrovietnam chairman Le Manh Hung asked PV Gas to triple Thi Vai's capacity to 3 mtpa; PV Gas said preparations were essentially complete and it expected to sign/award the EPC contract in late 2025. TTCL performed the FEED design and EPC tender preparation (scope: raising total send-out to 3 MMTPA including the existing 1 MMTPA terminal). No EPC award or construction start had been announced as of early July 2026.

topic: March 2026 grid-connection agreement; COD re-targeted to 2030
wiki_text: On March 10, 2026, Bac Lieu LNG Power Company (Delta Offshore Energy) and Vietnam's National Power Transmission Corporation (EVNNPT) signed the principal agreement on grid connection for the 3,200 MW Bac Lieu LNG-to-power project, covering evacuation via a 500 kV Bac Lieu-Thot Not line. Phased commercial operation is targeted for 2030 (Unit 1 March, Unit 2 June, Unit 3 September, Unit 4 December). The project, Vietnam's first fully privately financed integrated LNG-to-power scheme, remains pre-FID; construction, once planned for 2024, has not begun.

The VinaCapital-GS Energy Long An LNG-to-power complex (investment certificate March 2021, originally targeted for operation in December 2025) has slipped repeatedly: Long An province's April 2024 implementation plan targeted commercial operation of Long An I in June 2028 and Long An II in June 2031, while GS Energy said in February 2025 it aimed to operate from 2029. In December 2025 Vietnam's prime minister ordered resolution of bottlenecks in PPA negotiations, gas supply agreements, financing and investment procedures; the feasibility study had passed Electricity Authority appraisal and a preliminary grid-connection agreement with EVNNPT was in preparation.
